$Comment: The one look every HUD card is drawn in: the colour and the transparency of the card's frame,
as a single hex. A card is any panel wearing the shared frame: the Activity ledger and the
World bars (Server/ZiggfreedCommon/HudBarPanels/), the quest tracker, and a mod's own panel
built on the same base (RPG Stations' session summary reads this file too).
Color MULTIPLIES the shipped frame texture, so #ffffff is exactly the shipped look, a darker
hex darkens the frame and a hue tints it: #806040 is a warm brown card, #405060 a cool one.
Eight digits carry a transparency in the last two, so #ffffffb8 is the shipped card at about
72 percent, #ffffff80 at half and #ffffff40 at a quarter; six digits is fully opaque. The
shipped value below is the identity, and a card left at it is drawn exactly as its document
says. Text, icons and the bars' fills keep their own colours whatever the card wears.
This ONE file dims or colours every card at once. To treat one card differently, give it a
Color of its own: a bar spot's file (Server/ZiggfreedCommon/HudBarPlacements/) colours
whichever panel sits there, a bar panel's file (Server/ZiggfreedCommon/HudBarPanels/) colours
that panel wherever it sits and wins over the spot's, and a mod's own settings colour its own
panel; each falls back to this file when it states none. On the bar panels the well behind
each fill, the gloss across it and the shade under it follow the card's transparency on their
own, keeping their colours, so a dimmed panel keeps reading as a set of bars.
To change it without copying this file, add an entry keyed 'Default' to
mods/ziggfreedcommon/hud-cards.json: { "Default": { "Color": "#ffffffb8" } }. A value
that is not a #rrggbb or #rrggbbaa hex is ignored with one line in the log naming it.
